research.job_description_summary: JPMorgan Chase hires technology analysts in India through the Software Engineer Program and the Code for Good hackathon. A February 2026 JobRise guide (no cited candidate sources) describes a 60 to 90 minute HackerRank assessment with 2 coding problems and MCQs on Java, DBMS and OS, a technical phone screen, Super Day rounds on DSA, CS fundamentals and behavioral questions based on Business Principles, and an HR round. An August 2025 Jointaro intern account gives one coding question about filtering API queries. The official careers page was not fetched.
limitations: JPMorgan Chase's official careers page was not fetched, so no round is marked DOCUMENTED.
The February 2026 JobRise guide cites no candidate sources for its question list; everything based on it is class D (topic context).
The only candidate-attributed question is one Jointaro internship report (August 2025, Code for Good) about filtering API queries; one item is class B and unverified.

Glassdoor reviews found for 2026 were not India-tagged, listed no questions or described only a generic HireVue; they were not used. LeetCode posts found were for experienced SDE3 hires and were excluded.
Structure of the Software Engineer Program rounds is taken from the guide; the Code for Good hackathon format is not modelled.
System design items are extension questions; the guide lists system design for experienced roles only.

Evidence handling: practice questions cite no sources; where a source only supplied topic context it is named in the question notes. Practice and job-description-inferred questions are UNVERIFIED and capped at LOW confidence on import.

Review status: answers, samples and cited counts come from the researcher and were not independently re-run; spot checks only. Source titles and some dates are blank because the sources did not show them.
